resources.string: Scan nearby Bluetooth devices. Tap one to track its signal, long-press to rename it.
Searching for nearby Bluetooth devices…\nMake sure the lost device is powered on (advertising).

Hold the phone about one meter (a big step) away from the device and keep still. The app samples the signal for 3 seconds, so distance estimates for this device become far more accurate than the generic default.
Calibrated: 1 m ≈ %1$d dBm. Distance estimates for this device are now much more accurate.
Signal too weak or unstable. Get closer to the device and try again.

Hold the phone flat against your chest, screen facing away from you, then slowly turn a full circle in place. Your body blocks the signal from behind you, so the direction with the strongest signal is where the device is. The white triangle shows the direction you are facing — aim it at the green arrow.
Not sampled yet — start turning slowly
Strongest: %1$s (low confidence — reflections likely, try another circle)
Hold the phone upright in front of you (as if reading it) and walk around normally. Your path is drawn and colored by signal strength — the greenest stretch is where you were closest to the device.
Beep faster as you get closer (no need to watch the screen)

Tips:
· Move slowly — half a meter at a time, pause 2 seconds and watch the trend arrow
· Every +6 dBm roughly halves the distance
· Rotate the phone slowly; one direction will show a clearly stronger signal
· Walls, metal and your own body all attenuate the signal a lot
· The distance estimate is only approximate — trust the trend arrow and color zones
Bluetooth permissions are required to scan. Grant them in system settings and retry.
Android 11 and below require the location service to be on for Bluetooth scanning (this app never reads your location).
This phone does not support Bluetooth
